   Board of Library Trustees Agenda Report

Meeting Date:  November 5, 2024
From:  Daniel Calleros, Interim City Administrator
Department:  City Administration
Submitted by:  Karla Washington, Management Analyst

Subject
Vernon Reads! Virtual Library Program

Recommendation
A. Approve the Vernon Reads! Virtual Library Program (Program) and recommend that City
Council allocate $25,000 in funding to establish a budget for the purchase of e-readers, e-book
subscriptions and online resources in support of literacy for Fiscal Year 2024-25 and subsequent
fiscal years; and
B. Authorize any unused funds allocated to the Program to be used for the purchase of physical
books.

Background
At its June 2, 2020 meeting, the Board of Library Trustees established the Library Ad Hoc
Committee to work with staff to determine a plan to reestablish the Vernon Public Library. Since
then, the Library Ad Hoc Committee has worked with staff to explore various opportunities for the
provision of library services through creative means such as establishing a Little Free Libraries
Program in the City. In consultation with the Library Ad Hoc Committee, currently comprised of
President Pro Tem Ybarra and Trustee Lopez, staff proposes the Vernon Reads! Virtual Library
Program (Program) to further facilitate and promote literacy in the City.

In the absence of traditional brick-and-mortar City-operated libraries, City staff has sought out
creative solutions to encourage literacy, make books available to the community, and inspire a
love of reading and learning. Research suggests that American children are reading for leisure
at a declining rate compared to children in prior decades. Researchers also found that reading
for pleasure is becoming less popular amongst adults, and those who still read for pleasure are
reading less per day.

The Vernon Reads! Virtual Library Program (Program) would address such challenges by
providing subscriptions for e-book services to Vernon residents, and Amazon Kindle e-readers
with Kids+ Kindle Unlimited e-book subscriptions to TK-12th grade students living in Vernon. E-
readers further encourage reading because they allow readers easy access to a library of books
on a single device, with the added benefit of an integrated dictionary and language translation.
Students will have regular on-going access to age-appropriate books, allowing them the
opportunity to choose books based on their favorite genre or mood. The Kindle Kids e-reader
costs $115 and includes a 2-year “worry-free” warranty and 1-year subscription service. The
subscription provides access to thousands of e-books and audiobooks. The e-reader devices
offer distraction-free reading as they do not have apps, videos, or games. Ongoing annual
subscriptions are less than $100 annually.

For adult readers in the City, the Program would provide subscriptions to Everand (formerly
known as Scribd) which provides access to millions of e-books, audiobooks, and magazines at
a cost of $119 annually. Studies show that recreational reading for adults is an effective way to
manage stress and has benefits for concentration, vocabulary, writing skills, and memory. The
Program will not provide e-readers for adults as Everand is available as an app for Android and

  Item 2  Page 6 of 9
 Apple operating system devices, making books accessible on mobile phones, tablets and
computers. For adult readers, staff proposes a budget of $9,000 for approximately 75
subscriptions to Everand. Digital reading services vary as do individual reading habits. After
considerable research, staff proposes Amazon’s Kindle Unlimited and Everand e-book services
based on their available content and accessibility. The Program may offer other digital reading
services in the future as subscription services improve or become more widely available.

To participate in the Program, Vernon residents must submit an enrollment form (see attachment
1 for reference). And, once enrolled, families that enjoy their e-reader subscriptions can apply
with the City for an annual renewal. City staff will purchase annual subscriptions that residents
can redeem with Amazon for their renewal. The annual re-application process ensures that the
City only pays for subscriptions that are being used. Renewals in subsequent fiscal years would
be based on available funding allocations for the Program approved by the City Council during
the annual budget process.

Additional virtual reading/learning resources include a new City webpage with links to resources
provided by LA County Public Library, serving residents of all cities in LA County. City staff will
continue to work with LA County Library to participate in Vernon City events to raise awareness
and connect residents with educational resources being provided by the LA County Library,
including homework assistance, resume, and job application assistance, as well as signing up
for library cards to access books and in-person resources available at the Huntington Park and
Maywood branches of the LA County Library. Future program goals include the evaluation of
additional virtual learning resources such as Coursera, BrainFuse, and Creative Bug.

To further support the program’s goal of encouraging a love of reading, literacy, and learning,
future library program updates will focus on increasing access to physical books, which will be
achieved in multiple ways. First, through donating new books to the public for personal book
ownership in support of “home libraries” and creating a “Community Book Nook” at City Hall. City
staff is evaluating options for building bookshelves outside Council Chambers, around the stairs
and along the back wall. This location would provide the community convenient access to books
during City events and make use of un-utilized space. Current estimates for custom shelving
were over $50,000. City staff continues to explore other vendors and alternative publicly
accessible locations. Books at the Book Nook are proposed to be a combination of new and
preowned books and would function like the City’s Little Libraries, where the community can take
books to keep or return.

Books for the Program would be acquired in several ways, including purchased with City funds,
purchased with grant funds as well as acquired through donations from non-profit organizations
and City partners like Libros Schmibros, who has already donated over a dozen boxes of pre-
owned books to the City. In addition to building the Book Nook, staff proposes that the City also
give away new books at City events, organize reading contests during Summer and Winter
school breaks, and provide prizes for reading achievements.

The benefits of childhood reading are well known, but reading has so many lesser-known benefits
for adults, including:

  •  Stress reduction: Reading can reduce stress levels by up to 68%. It can help you relax by
  slowing your breathing and relaxing your muscles.
  •  Brain connectivity: Reading can improve brain connectivity.
  •  Lower blood pressure and heart rate: Reading can lower your blood pressure and heart
  rate.

  Item 2  Page 7 of 9
   •  Depression symptom fighting: Reading can help fight depression symptoms.
  •  Cognitive decline prevention: Reading can help prevent cognitive decline as you age.

The Vernon Reads! Virtual Library Program encourages reading as a lifelong skill that improves
memory, builds a robust vocabulary, and builds a foundation of knowledge and significant
physical and mental health benefits for Vernon residents of all ages.

Fiscal Impact
Approval of the Program would require an appropriation by the City Council of $25,000 for the
purchase of e-readers, e-reader subscriptions, and books in General Fund, Community
Development, Good Neighbor Program Account No. 011-010-160-529715 from available
Unassigned Fund Balance. The Board of Library Trustees recommends the City Council allocate
said funds.
